decisions.decision: Use scheduled batch scoring for document classification
decisions.context: The system classifies millions of documents daily, and several teams consume its results. The brief gives no requirement for request-time predictions.

alternatives.label: Online computation serving
cons: Does not match a stated latency need

decisions.rationale: It fits the stated volume and shared result consumption. Netflix’s “System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation” and “Scalable Software and Big Data Architecture” describe scheduled scoring and stored results; the checked rival point using online serving was attested by one source, while this combination was unattested.
consequences: Classification freshness depends on the scoring schedule.

decisions.decision: Scale runtime resources elastically with workload demand
decisions.context: Document volume varies strongly over the year, so fixed capacity risks either peak-time bottlenecks or unused capacity outside peaks.
decisions.rationale: Elastic scaling addresses seasonal variation directly. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” support scaling resources with workload demand; the checked design point returned no conflicting warnings.
consequences: Capacity must be monitored as demand changes.
Resource use and cost will vary with workload.

decisions.decision: Monitor input and feature drift in production
decisions.context: Operators need visibility into quality drift, and changes in incoming documents can affect classifier behavior. Monitoring practices can be combined because this dimension has low exclusivity in the design space.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Drift does not prove quality loss

alternatives.label: Real-time prediction-quality monitoring
cons: Quality issues may appear after delay

decisions.rationale: Drift monitoring provides operators a direct signal when incoming data changes; “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and Google Cloud’s “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support monitoring inputs and features. Add prediction-quality monitoring when labels become available; it is compatible as a combined practice, though the point checker accepts only one value per dimension and the batch-plus-drift-plus-elastic point was unattested.
consequences: Monitoring needs baselines for expected inputs.
Drift alerts require investigation before retraining.

uncovered: How document data is ingested, retained, and governed, including insurer privacy and access controls.
How classifier labels and model quality are evaluated, and how false positives and false negatives are weighted.
How scoring schedules, freshness targets, and workload partitioning are set.
How classification outputs are versioned and delivered consistently to consuming teams.
How model changes are approved, deployed, and rolled back.
